prompt: In many countries, young people are granted certain privileges and responsibilities at the age of 16. Clearly, parents have a responsibility to both care for and prepare their children as they approach this important milestone. To what degree should parents intervene in the lives of their 15-year-old children? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
In many countries, young people are given more rights and responsibilities when they reach the age of 16. Therefore, many people believe that parents should prepare their children before they reach this important age. This essay argues that parents should guide their 15-year-old children to a certain extent while also allowing them enough freedom to become independent.

Parents should continue to guide their children because teenagers at the age of 15 are not mature enough to make every decision on their own. The first thing is that parents can help them distinguish between right, wrong and protect them from harmful influences such as bad friendships or unhealthy habits. As a result, teenagers are more likely to make responsible decisions. For example, if a 15-year-old wants to stay out with friends on school nights, parents should explain the consequences and set reasonable rules instead of allowing complete freedom. Therefore, appropriate parental guidance helps teenagers develop responsibility and self-discipline.

However, parents should not control every aspect of their children’s lives because teenagers also need opportunities to become independent. They should be encouraged to make their own choices in areas such as managing their study time, choosing hobbies or solving small personal problems. This allows them to learn from both success and failure and prepare for adult life. For instance, parents can let their children decide how to organise their weekly study schedule instead of planning every hour for them. Teenagers gradually become more confident and capable of making decisions by themselves.

In conclusion, I believe that parents should intervene in the lives of their 15 years old children only to a reasonable degree. By providing guidance while respecting their independence, parents can help teenagers become responsible and confident adults.
